what_happened: After a container reset, the fresh clone of Athena's working copy had no origin/HEAD ref. The baseline-reuse step finds main's CI result through that ref, so every baseline ran locally instead of reusing main's CI run. The person running Athena ran `git remote set-head origin main` by hand. No job was rejected or failed, and no acceptance criterion, check or finding failed. This is an environment gap, and it is a repeat of the one fixed by hand on 2026-11-04.
cause: Athena's setup and startup neither create origin/HEAD nor check that it exists. The baseline-reuse lookup treats a missing ref as "no baseline to reuse" and quietly runs the full baseline. A fresh clone, such as after a container reset, therefore starts without the ref and the failure looks like normal slow behavior. The first fix, on 2026-11-04, was a one-off hand command and did not make the clone setup repeatable. The state is lost whenever the checkout is rebuilt.
other_causes: Nothing reports at the time of a baseline that reuse was skipped and why, so the gap shows only as lost speed.
Container resets recreate the clone, and nothing in the reset path restores hand-set clone state.
open_hypotheses: Whether the earlier case's fix, if any, landed in code, or whether only the hand command was ever applied. The fields do not say.
How many baselines ran locally before the the person running Athena noticed. The fields do not give a count.
prevention: At startup, and before each baseline, Athena should check for origin/HEAD. If it is missing, Athena should set it with `git remote set-head origin --auto` or from the configured main branch, so a fresh clone is always correct. If the ref cannot be set, Athena should print a clear warning and record that baseline reuse was skipped. A test should start from a clone without origin/HEAD and show that reuse is found after setup. That closes the whole class of unchecked clone state falling back to the slow path.
proposed_request: Make baseline reuse robust to a clone that has no origin/HEAD. Outcome: in a fresh clone (for example after a container reset), Athena creates origin/HEAD pointing at the main branch itself, at startup or before the first baseline. It then finds main's CI result and reuses it with no hand command. If the ref cannot be created, Athena says so in the output and records that the baseline reuse was skipped, with the reason, instead of silently running the full baseline. Acceptance: (1) a test that starts from a clone with origin/HEAD removed shows that the baseline is reused after Athena's own setup; (2) a test where the ref cannot be set shows the warning and the recorded skip reason; (3) add a CHANGELOG.md entry.
